top_three.content_snippet:
I knew things were a little off when the first thing I heard on my walk to the AI Music Awards was “the winner…” followed by the sweet voice of Kelly Clarkson.

To qualify for the awards, artists needed to register their tracks to SIQA’s “Verified Registry,” which denotes whether the song was fully AI-generated, made with the assistance of AI or featured a cloned human voice to lead the tune (what the group calls a “human + AI hybrid”).

Registered artists then nominate their peers in the 25 cat
top_three.summary_en: The inaugural AI Music Awards took place in Los Angeles, hosted by the Sonic Intelligence Academy, which implemented a 'Verified Registry' to categorize entries into fully AI-generated, AI-assisted, and human-AI hybrid works. This initiative aims to establish an infrastructure comparable to the Recording Academy, seeking industry legitimacy for AI music creators amidst ongoing legal disputes over copyright infringement.

Megaspeed shipped the chips to buyers in China who maintained long-standing business ties with local tech giants, the WSJ reports. The orders covered several hundred thousand chips that the US had sought to
top_three.summary_en: Megaspeed, a cloud service provider, brokered approximately $12 billion worth of high-performance Nvidia AI chip orders for Chinese clients between March 2024 and June 2025. Leveraging its status as an official Nvidia cloud partner, the firm—owned by Alice Huang—facilitated the bypass of US export controls by supplying restricted silicon to Chinese tech entities through indirect channels.

topic_focus.summary_en: Following allegations of circumventing US export sanctions via Southeast Asian data centers, Jensen Huang was abruptly ousted from Nvidia. Key shareholders Altimeter and Atreides ($2.13B stake) sent an urgent board letter demanding his return, while an Elon Musk-backed petition exceeded 100K signatures, triggering panic over collapsing open-source model subsidies.

linked_tweets.author: CHIIIDEX 💔💔
linked_tweets.content_zh:
经过充分训练的人工智能模型并不意味着它不再需要计算能力。

训练教会模型如何识别模式、理解语言和生成响应。

但每次有人使用该模型时，它仍然需要计算资源来处理请求并产生答案，这称为推理。

想象一下数百万人同时使用 ChatGPT、生成图像、编写代码和运行 AI 代理。每次交互都需要处理能力。

与训练不同，推理是一个持续的过程。当模型发布时它并没有停止。

这就是人工智能公司继续投资数十亿美元建设数据中心和数千个 GPU 的原因。

构建智能模型是一项挑战。拥有足够的计算能力来服务世界是另一回事。
linked_tweets.content_en:
An AI model being fully trained doesn’t mean it stops needing computing power.

Training teaches the model how to recognize patterns, understand language, and generate responses. 

But every time someone uses that model, it still needs computing resources to process the request and produce an answer., This is called inference.

Think about millions of people using ChatGPT simultaneously, generating images, writing code, and running AI agents. Every interaction requires processing power.

Unlike training, inference is an ongoing process. It doesn’t stop when the model is released.

This is why AI companies continue investing billions in data centers and thousands of GPUs.

Building an intelligent model is one challenge. Having enough computing power to serve the world is another.

“该图像是由四个完全独立的场景组成的 2x2 网格，每个场景正好填充图像的四分之一（每个四分之一本身就是一张 16:9 的图片），由完全笔直的纯白色排水沟划分，一个垂直向下，一个水平穿过正中心。”
- 然后描述左上、右上、左下和右下场景。
- 在中心附近最亮的白色行和列上分割每个四边形，在线条保持超过 60% 的白色时走出去，然后再修剪 6 像素。
- 在 1920x1080 下将每个图块裁剪为 16:9。
- 物体特写可以成为很棒的图块：一张桌子、一个屏幕、一份文件、一盘食物、一个金库。
3.主要人物，2-3人。为每个角色写一个固定的描述（年龄、头发、脸、每件衣服的颜色），然后逐字粘贴到每张纸上。

- 表情表：6 个无臂正面（希望、厌恶、恐惧、疲惫、生病、震惊或脚本需要的任何内容），以基础表作为参考。
- 姿势表：6 个带有道具的完整姿势（坐在办公桌前打字、睡觉、吃饭、跑步、签名、摔倒），以基础表作为参考。
4. 其他人：4-6 人的角色表，每个人都按照他们的拍摄需要的准确姿势绘制； 8-10 个小数字的人群表；道具表。
- 每张纸：“在坚实的平坦色度绿色背景上（#00B140），人物之间有很多空白的绿色空间；没有任何接触，任何角色或物体上没有任何东西是绿色的，全身，没有被边缘切断的东西”。
5.缩略图艺术：相同的角色，具有更丰富的饱和卡通灯光和极端的情感，上四分之一留空，没有文字，以底纸为参考。
</艺术>

<装备>
剪纸：
- 背景是 G - max(R,B) 超过 40 且在中值绿色 110 以内的每个边界连接像素。钥匙只能从边框处，否则深色衣服会漏。
- 添加 2 px 软 alpha 带并将 G 钳位到其中的 max(R,B) + 6，这会消除绿色边缘。
- 按图形和掉落斑点对碎片进行分组。给每个精灵命名，然后给我看一张命名的联系表。

无臂的正面人物变成了木偶：
- 将头部在颈部分开：头部下方最窄的 alpha 行。
- 找到肩窝和眼窝。
- 用身体本身的颜色修补头下的洞，这样点头就不会出现间隙。
- 将所有内容写入 rig.js：尺寸、颈部、插座、眼框、皮肤 RGB、袖子 RGB。
- 手臂：上L1约为人物高度的0.13，下L2约为0.12，厚度约为0.04。对肘部和前臂皮肤使用袖子颜色，当手臂位于身体后方时，使用 0.82 倍深的袖子，以及圆形帽和连接处。
- 手：三种形状的连指手套（手套、张开、拳头），加上一根手指伸出的点。
- 手臂姿势：每个都是相对于肩膀的手部目标，单位为L = L1 + L2，通过二骨IK解决（其中有两个标志，第一个是左臂）。
- 向下：(∓0.04, 0.97)
- 休息：（±0.1，0.9）
- 臀部：(∓0.42, 0.55) 用拳头
- 点：右手到（0.86，-0.32）
- 现在：右手到（0.75，0.25），打开
- 耸肩：(∓0.62, 0.12)，打开
- 向上：(∓0.32，-0.9)
- 双手放在头上
- 下巴：拳头放在脖子上
- 保持：（±0.42，0.45）
- 波：（0.5，-0.75）
- 停止：(0.55，-0.1)
- 欢呼：（∓0.55，-0.75）用拳头
- 姿势变化在 0.3-0.5 秒内通过缓入缓出混合两个目标。
- 侧面、背面和姿势精灵保持完整图像。只有头部转动，绘图或打字的手抖动±6 px。
</钻>

<动画>
一个 HTML 画布，其中每一帧都是时间 t 的纯函数：window .seek(t)、READY、END 和 EV，按名称列出的声音事件列表。
- 将每个镜头挂在旁白上：S('exact Words', fn) 在该短语之前 0.08 秒开始一个镜头。重复的单词按出现次数查找。
- 每个镜头一个功能，每个章节一个镜头文件。

运动基元（Δ = t - 开始）：
- 弹出：0.3 秒后缓超调，1 + 2.9(p-1)^3 + 1.9(p-1)^2。
- 弹簧输入：1 - e^(-6.5Δ) cos(13Δ)。
- 冲击力踢：1 + 0.1 e^(-10Δ) cos(22Δ)。
- 摇动：x = A e^(-8Δ) sin(61Δ)，y = A e^(-8Δ) cos(47Δ)。
- 退出时间随着缓入时间的延长而缩小，时间超过 0.25 秒。事物到来时会伴随着春天、南瓜或白色的泡芙，而不是简单的褪色。

相机：
- camP（plate，zoom，fx，fy）将视图保持在板边缘内。
- 每个镜头都会通过缓入、2-4% 的推力或缓慢的平移从一个 [zoom、fx、fy] 移动到另一个，因此没有什么是静止的。
- 在同一相机变换内绘制盘子及其上的所有内容。
- 将四块图块上的缩放保持在 1.33 倍以下。仅在英雄板块上进行更深入的缩放。

过渡：
- 推：旧镜头从左侧滑出，新镜头从右侧滑入，0.24 秒缓入，之前有 0.02 秒的嗖嗖声。
- 章节 splat：#f4f1fb 斑点在 0.2 秒内覆盖屏幕并在 0.2 秒内清除。它是一个 1,250 像素的圆圈，由 12 个黄金角间距的大卫星斑点和更远的 10 个小水滴组成，在进入时向左移动 120 像素，在离开时向右移动 140 像素。

每一帧都充满活力的人物：
- 呼吸：标度 1 + 0.009 sin(2.3t)。
- 点头：0.025 sin(2.1t) rad，或 0.025 sin(7t) + 0.02 sin(11.3t)，同时说出该角色的台词。
- 闪烁：每 2.7-4.2 秒，每个数字播种。在 0.14 秒内，用弯曲的睫毛线将每个眼框涂上肤色。
- 步行：
- 鲍勃|罪|位于人物高度的 2.2% 处，主体岩石为 ±0.035 rad。
- 侧视行走精灵每个步循环滑动 1.5 条腿长，因此脚不会滑行。
- 进入泉水，有时会跳跃。恐惧是一种快速的震动（sin 70t）。惊喜是一个跳跃和一个橙色的“！”。
- 每个人物下方都有一个柔和的接触阴影椭圆。夜间拍摄的照片会用亮度 (1 - k) 使它们变暗，因此它们与车牌相匹配。
- 屏幕上的每个角色都按照自己的路线行事：指向被命名的事物，展示它，耸肩，欢呼，抬起头。
</动画>

<图形>
文本只存在于世界上的事物上，逐个字母地输入：每秒 28 个字母（短标签为 34 个）。每个字母以 1.45 倍大和向右 0.7 倍高度开始，并在 0.18 秒内稳定下来并缓出。

完整套件：
- 板：白色圆形板（半径 20），在弹簧上下降 420 px，摆动 0.25 rad 到位，或者站在木柱上，从 -1 rad 向上摆动。

- 输入的行之间间隔 0.3 秒。
- 日期卡：左上角 (70, 70)，白色，高 120 像素，宽至少 330 像素，半径 18。橙色日历图标，26 像素处有灰色“日期：”，以 44 像素粗细 900 输入日期。弹出时间超过 0.32 秒。

- 橙子 ”？”它在一个困惑的头上晃动和摇摆，还有一个橙色的“！”流行音乐。
- 白色的云彩、速度线、浅蓝色的汗滴、硬币和钞票、柔和的小插图以及适合心情的色调。
- 只要该地方有空白板、屏幕和页面，就可以在该板块自己的空白板、屏幕和页面上书写。首先在板的网格覆盖层上测量毛坯的矩形。
</图形>

<声音>
- ElevenLabs：深度、温暖的美国纪录片旁白，eleven_v4，稳定性0.5，相似度0.75，风格0，扬声器增强，带有时间戳端点。

- 运行速度更快，在构建图片之前仔细研究结果并将其与脚本进行比较。
- 免费路线：Kokoro，然后更快地耳语单词时间。
</语音>

<声音>
- 音乐：Pixabay 上的 2-3 张免费纪录片床，以大节奏交叉淡入淡出超过 3 秒。
- 将音乐隐藏在声音下方（30 毫秒起音，0.3 秒保持，0.45 秒释放）并让它在章节之间回升。
- 来自 Mixkit 的 SFX，每个事件一个，按峰值对齐，语音时安静 6 dB：打字时的打字声、推动和敲击时的呼啸声、标签和卡片上的流行声、邮票上的重击声、每个红色 X 上的敲击声、滴答声上的叮当声，以及适合场景的声音。
- 门限：在演讲期间，声音比音乐加 SFX（100 毫秒帧的中值）高 15+ dB，并且背景比帧中的声音大 1%。
- 两次通过响度至 -14 LUFS，真实峰值 -1 dB。
</声音>

<构建>
1. 工具：Python、Playwright with Chromium 或 Edge、FFmpeg、faster-whisper、OpenCV、Pillow、numpy。安装缺少的内容并告诉我您安装了哪些内容。
2、订购：
- 外观测试
- 分批创作，每批之后都有一张联系表
- 剪裁和装备
- 语音和单词时间
- 镜头，逐章
3. 在任何完整渲染之前进行检查：每章一张联系表，每 2 秒一帧。修复：
- 空的或溢出的标志
- 脸上的文字
- 黑色板边缘
- 脚浮离地板
- 在同一个地方连续射击两次
- 任何没有新内容到达的 4 秒
4. 以 30 fps 渲染，半帧上有 4 个运动模糊子帧，帧通过管道输送到 libx264 CRF 16-18。
- 将长视频分割到 4-6 个并行浏览器页面并连接各个部分。
- 扫描单帧跳转的结果并检查每一帧是否是计划的剪切。
</构建>

<陷阱>
- 读起来很懒的地方太少了。一个盘子能保持 30 秒，上面有卡片，看起来很便宜。预算大约每分钟 10 个新位置。
- 一些图像模型忽略“没有手臂”。 GPT 图片 2 紧随其后。
- 将相同的角色描述粘贴到每张纸中，然后将底纸放回原处，否则脸部和衣服会漂移。
- 四块图块的宽度仅为约 1920 像素。突破 1.33 倍看起来很软。
- 已经画有人物的图版无法进行动画处理。切割前要求清空并检查。
- 漂浮在艺术作品上方的卡片上的文字看起来像幻灯片。写下这个世界。
- 长时间渲染崩溃。渲染可以重新运行的部分，并在每个大补丁之前备份镜头文件。
</陷阱>

<开始>
询问我的主题、剧本、形象模型和声音，然后进行外观测试。
</开始>

Camera:
- camP(plate, zoom, fx, fy) keeps the view inside the plate's edges.
- Every shot moves from one [zoom, fx, fy] to another with ease-in-out, a 2-4% push or a slow pan, so nothing holds still.
- Draw the plate and everything on it inside the same camera transform.
- Keep zoom under 1.33x on quad tiles. Zoom deeper only on hero plates.

Transitions:
- Push: the old shot slides out left while the new one slides in from the right, 0.24 s ease-in-out, with a whoosh 0.02 s before.
- Chapter splat: a #f4f1fb blob covers the screen in 0.2 s and clears in 0.2 s. It's a 1,250 px circle, 12 big satellite blobs at golden-angle spacing and 10 small droplets further out, shifted 120 px left on the way in and 140 px right on the way out.

Characters, alive in every frame:
- Breathing: scale 1 + 0.009 sin(2.3t).
- Head nod: 0.025 sin(2.1t) rad, or 0.025 sin(7t) + 0.02 sin(11.3t) while that character's line is spoken.
- Blink: every 2.7-4.2 s, seeded per figure. For 0.14 s, paint each eye box over in skin colour with a curved lash line.
- Walk:
  - Bob |sin| at 2.2% of the figure's height, with a body rock of ±0.035 rad.
  - Side-view walk sprites slide 1.5 leg lengths per step cycle, so the feet don't skate.
- Enter on the spring, sometimes with a hop. Fear is a fast shake (sin 70t). Surprise is a jump and an orange "!".
- A soft contact shadow ellipse under every figure. Night shots darken them with brightness(1 - k), so they match the plate.
- Every character on screen acts on its line: points at the thing being named, presents it, shrugs, cheers, holds its head.
</animation>

<graphics>
Text only lives on things in the world, typed letter by letter: 28 letters a second (34 for short tags). Each letter starts 1.45x big and 0.7 em to the right and settles in 0.18 s with ease-out.

The full kit:
- Board: a white rounded board (radius 20) that drops 420 px on the spring and swings 0.25 rad into place, or stands on a wooden post and swings up from -1 rad.
  - Soft drop shadow (blur 22, y 8, 22%) and a faint darker strip along its bottom edge.
  - Lines typed 0.3 s apart.
- Date card: top left at (70, 70), white, 120 px tall, at least 330 px wide, radius 18. An orange calendar icon, a grey "DATE:" at 26 px, the date typed at 44 px weight 900. Pops in over 0.32 s.
- Place card: the same card with a red map pin and "PLACE:".
- Tag: a 6 px line with a dot at the thing, drawn in 0.2 s, then a rounded pill (the text at 40 px weight 900) pops on its end. Ink, red, gold or orange pills.
- Number card: a white card with a small grey label and a big red number. Long numbers roll up like a counter with ease-out.
- Red X: two round 30 px strokes, 0.11 s each, 0.01 s apart, with a soft shadow. One goes over every wrong idea.
- Stamp: red text in a double rounded border, tilted -0.12 rad. It slams from 2.1x to 1x in 0.14 s, then kicks.
- Banner: a full-width headline band, 92 px white caps on tomato or purple, rotated -0.02 rad, sliding in from the left over 0.22 s.
- Speech bubble: white, radius 36, with a tail. Thought cloud: a pill with two small circles.
- Orange "?" that bobs and sways over a puzzled head, and an orange "!" pop.
- White puff and poof clouds, speed lines, light blue sweat drops, coins and bills, a soft vignette, and a colour tint for mood.
- Write on the plate's own blank boards, screens and pages whenever the place has them. Measure the blank's rectangle on a grid overlay of the plate first.
</graphics>

<voice>
- ElevenLabs: a deep, warm US documentary narrator, eleven_v4, stability 0.5, similarity 0.75, style 0, speaker boost, with the timestamps endpoint.
- About 170-180 words a minute, using the voice's own speed setting (1.0-1.1). Never speed it up with atempo: it sounds chipmunked.
- Long scripts go in 3 chunks split at chapter breaks, passing the previous and next text so the read stays continuous.
- Cut pauses over 0.24 s to 0.16 s, leave 0.5 s at chapter breaks, and add a 0.3 s lead-in.
- Rebuild word times from the alignment into words.js.
- Run faster-whisper over the result and diff it against the script before building the picture.
- Free route: Kokoro, then faster-whisper for the word times.
</voice>

<sound>
- Music: 2-3 free documentary beds from Pixabay, crossfaded over 3 s at big beats.
- Duck the music under the voice (30 ms attack, 0.3 s hold, 0.45 s release) and let it swell back up between chapters.
- SFX from Mixkit, one per event, aligned by their peaks, 6 dB quieter on speech: a typewriter tick on typing, a whoosh on pushes and splats, a pop on tags and cards, a thud on stamps, a hit on every red X, a ding on ticks, plus sounds that fit the scene.
- Gate: during speech the voice sits 15+ dB over music plus SFX (median of 100 ms frames), and the background is louder than the voice in under 1% of frames.
- Two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS, true peak -1 dB.
</sound>

<build>
1. Tools: Python, Playwright with Chromium or Edge, FFmpeg, faster-whisper, OpenCV, Pillow, numpy. Install what's missing and tell me what you installed.
2. Order:
   - the look test
   - the art in batches, with a contact sheet after each
   - cutouts and rig
   - voice and word times
   - shots, chapter by chapter
3. Check before any full render: a contact sheet per chapter, one frame every 2 s. Fix:
   - empty or overflowing signs
   - text over a face
   - black plate edges
   - feet floating off the floor
   - two shots in a row in the same place
   - any 4 s where nothing new arrives
4. Render at 30 fps, 4 motion-blur subframes over half a frame, frames piped to libx264 CRF 16-18.
   - Split long videos across 4-6 parallel browser pages and join the parts.
   - Scan the result for single-frame jumps and check that each one is a planned cut.
</build>

<gotchas>
- Too few places reads as lazy. One plate held for 30 s with cards over it looks cheap. Budget about 10 new places a minute.
- Some image models ignore "no arms". GPT Image 2 follows it.
- Paste the same character description into every sheet and feed the base sheet back in, or faces and clothes drift.
- Quad tiles are only about 1920 px wide. Pushing past 1.33x looks soft.
- Plates with people already drawn in can't be animated. Ask for EMPTY and check before cutting.
- Text on a card floating over the art looks like a slideshow. Write on the world.
- Long renders crash. Render in parts you can rerun, and back up the shot files before every big patch.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for my topic, my script, my image model and my voice, then make the look test.
</start>

linked_tweets.author: nelson
linked_tweets.content_zh:
人工智能代理经济中最有趣的发展之一是代理雇佣其他代理来完成工作。

@termix_ai 最近通过 Montage Studio 在 上展示了这一点。

这是它的工作原理。

您提交视频制作简介。 Montage Studio 将其分解为更小的工作，并聘请专门的代理来处理故事板、视频渲染和音乐。

然后，它协调他们的工作，合并结果并交付完成的视频。

每个作业都经过 TermiX 上的托管。

这表明代理人如何承担更大的任务，外包专门工作并支付其他代理人的贡献。

但这需要的不仅仅是沟通。代理商需要发现服务、商定价格、确保付款、验证交付和处理纠纷。

这就是 TermiX 的代理自主商务协议 (AACP) 的用武之地。

其工作流程将流程整合在一起：

托管→交付→质疑→结算。

借助 TermiX Skills，代理商还可以连接到市场、寻找工作并参与这些交易。

方向很明确：代理商正在超越孤立的任务，转向雇用、协调和支付其他代理商来完成更大的工作。

这就是 TermiX 正在建设的自主经济。

当代理商开始相互开展业务时，可靠的交易基础设施就变得至关重要。

#TermiX #AACP
linked_tweets.content_en:
one of the more interesting developments in the ai agent economy is agents hiring other agents to get work done.

@termix_ai recently showcased this through Montage Studio on https://t.co/9ReKMK2L7m.

here's how it works.

you submit a video production brief. Montage Studio breaks it into smaller jobs and hires specialized agents to handle the storyboard, video rendering and music.

it then coordinates their work, combines the results and delivers the finished video.

each job goes through escrow on TermiX.

this shows how agents can take responsibility for larger tasks, outsource specialized work and pay other agents for their contributions.

but this requires more than communication. agents need to discover services, agree on prices, secure payments, verify delivery and handle disputes.

that's where TermiX's Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP) comes in.

its workflow brings the process together:

escrow → delivery → challenge → settlement.

with TermiX Skills, agents can also connect to the marketplace, find work and participate in these transactions.

the direction is clear: agents are moving beyond isolated tasks towards hiring, coordinating and paying other agents to complete larger jobs.

that's the kind of autonomous economy TermiX is building towards.

when agents start doing business with each other, reliable transaction infrastructure becomes essential.

#TermiX #AACP

linked_tweets.author: Effie Kavoura 🔶
linked_tweets.content_zh:
在添加另一个人工智能代理之前，我会问一个问题。

该代理将改进哪些业务决策？

不是它可以自动化多少任务。演示看起来并不那么令人印象深刻。

工作完成后，公司会发生什么变化？
linked_tweets.content_en:
Before adding another AI agent, I'd ask one question.

What business decision will this agent improve?

Not how many tasks it can automate. Not how impressive the demo looks.

What changes for the company when the work is done?

news.title_en: Inside the first AI Music Awards in Los Angeles, featuring AI announcers, lip-syncing, and human stand-ins, as the ceremony was mired in technical issues (Corbin Bolies/Variety)

inline_images.caption: The Sonic Intelligence Academy
inline_images.alt: The Sonic Intelligence Academy

news.author: Variety
news.content_snippet:
I knew things were a little off when the first thing I heard on my walk to the AI Music Awards was “the winner…” followed by the sweet voice of Kelly Clarkson.

To qualify for the awards, artists needed to register their tracks to SIQA’s “Verified Registry,” which denotes whether the song was fully AI-generated, made with the assistance of AI or featured a cloned human voice to lead the tune (what the group calls a “human + AI hybrid”).

Registered artists then nominate their peers in the 25 cat
news.summary_en: The inaugural AI Music Awards took place in Los Angeles, hosted by the Sonic Intelligence Academy, which implemented a 'Verified Registry' to categorize entries into fully AI-generated, AI-assisted, and human-AI hybrid works. This initiative aims to establish an infrastructure comparable to the Recording Academy, seeking industry legitimacy for AI music creators amidst ongoing legal disputes over copyright infringement.

news.content_snippet:
YouTube Music is my music-streaming service of choice. And since I’m a software reporter, I always enable the beta features available through YouTube Labs, which include Beyond the Beat. YouTube’s AI DJ randomly interjects for about 30 seconds between songs, teeing up the vibe shift and providing context about the next track.

More listeners are encountering synthetic commentary built into their music streaming apps. While YouTube launched this experimental AI DJ in 2025, Spotify first introduce
news.summary_en: YouTube Music (via Beyond the Beat) and Spotify are expanding AI DJ tools designed to provide background context and commentary between tracks using generative audio. However, user feedback indicates these features frequently suffer from verbose filler, mispronunciation of niche artists, and factual inconsistencies, significantly undermining the immersive streaming experience.

news.title: Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China
news.title_en: Firm linked to Jensen Huang's ex-lover reportedly brokered nearly $12 billion in Nvidia chip orders for China
news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet: Megaspeed arranged nearly $12 billion worth of Nvidia high-performance chip orders for Chinese companies between March 2024 and June 2025, according to documents reviewed by the Wall Street Journal. The company is owned by Alice Huang, the former lover of since-ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Megaspeed shipped the chips to buyers in China who maintained long-standing business ties with local tech giants, the WSJ reports. The orders covered several hundred thousand chips that the US had sought to
news.summary_en: Megaspeed, a cloud service provider, brokered approximately $12 billion worth of high-performance Nvidia AI chip orders for Chinese clients between March 2024 and June 2025. Leveraging its status as an official Nvidia cloud partner, the firm—owned by Alice Huang—facilitated the bypass of US export controls by supplying restricted silicon to Chinese tech entities through indirect channels.

news.summary_zh: 云服务合作伙伴Megaspeed被曝在2024年3月至2025年6月间，向中国客户销售近120亿美元英伟达高性能芯片

【起因与机理】利用英伟达云合作伙伴的特许分配权，结合中国市场旺盛的算力需求及监管合规漏洞实现绕道出口
【关键数据与实测】Megaspeed利用云服务商特许权，违规向中国市场分流近120亿美元英伟达AI芯片。
【各方立场与态度】该交易量与英伟达财报披露的中国区收入存在显著差异，引发市场对其合规真实性的质疑。

[Key Metrics] Megaspeed brokered $12 billion in restricted Nvidia AI chips to China using cloud partnership access.

news.author: Wired AI
news.content_snippet:
You forgot to water the plant. Instead of seeing yellowing leaves, you see a cute plant-shaped pet on a tiny screen, looking sad and dejected. Maybe that'll give you the push you needed to grab the watering can. As you pour water into the soil, the plant pet on the screen gets excited and happy.

news.summary_en: Daehwa Kim, a PhD student at Carnegie Mellon's Future Interfaces Group, presented Object Agent Twins (OATs) at the ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology. The system integrates low-cost E Ink displays with sensors monitoring moisture, temperature, and motion, utilizing Google Gemini Nano to generate interactive AI avatars for physical objects.

【起因与机理】旨在减少用户对手机屏幕的依赖，将AI交互从虚拟场景引入物理环境

news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
AI has barely displaced any jobs in Australia so far, but young workers entering highly exposed fields like software development are faring worse.

An analysis by Mike Major for Australia's central bank (RBA) built a monitoring system that focuses on the areas where effects are likely to appear first, namely entry-level workers and highly AI-exposed occupations such as programming, clerical work, and customer service.

According to the analysis, job postings have fallen across all groups since C
news.summary_en: Mike Major, a researcher at the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), found that demand for entry-level roles in high-exposure sectors like software, customer service, and clerical work has structurally declined since late 2022. The data corroborates a global trend where AI-driven automation of repetitive tasks disproportionately hampers early-career employment, while senior-level positions remain relatively insulated.

news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
Meituan releases the weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter model built for AI agents. It was trained entirely on Chinese hardware and performs at the level US models like Claude Opus 5 reached a few months ago on coding benchmarks.

The LongCat team at Chinese food delivery company Meituan has released the weights for LongCat-2.5, one week after the model's official unveiling. LongCat-2.5 is built for agents that work through long, multi-step tasks autonomously, particularly coding.
news.summary_en: Meituan's LongCat team has released the LongCat-2.5 model, a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 1.6 trillion total parameters and approximately 48 billion active parameters per token. The model was trained entirely on domestic hardware without Nvidia GPUs, utilizing 4-bit quantization, and supports a million-token context window with multimodal capabilities.

【起因与机理】构建自主可控的AI Agent算力底座，解决复杂多步任务执行与长序列推理需求
【关键数据与实测】采用MoE混合专家架构，总参数量1.6万亿，激活参数480亿。

news.title: A post-Jensen Nvidia must reshuffle its leadership, reset its DC ties, and recognize that even the US' most valuable company cannot dictate US foreign policy (Chris Miller/Financial Times)
news.title_en: A post-Jensen Nvidia must reshuffle its leadership, reset its DC ties, and recognize that even the US' most valuable company cannot dictate US foreign policy (Chris Miller/Financial Times)
news.author: Financial Times
news.content_snippet: The chip company has only itself to blame for a long list of adversaries — Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia, the company he co-founded …
news.summary_en: Nvidia faces pressure to initiate leadership succession and restructure its Washington lobbying operations to navigate escalating geopolitical constraints. The imperative is to align corporate strategy with restrictive U.S. export controls, acknowledging that commercial hegemony cannot override national security mandates.
news.title_zh: 英伟达领导层与地缘战略的必要转型
news.summary_zh: 分析指出英伟达需重构领导架构并重塑华盛顿政商关系，以适应地缘政治对半导体产业主导权的强力约束
news.article_content_en:
Jensen Huang’s exit from Nvidia, the company he co-founded, after revelations of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is a humiliating end to an extraordinary career atop America’s AI sector. Yet his replacement will not end the investigations. The company’s remaining leaders will have to answer for staggering compliance failures that stretched beyond the CEO. And US President Donald Trump — until recently one of Huang’s biggest backers — will face intense pressure to increase his administration’s lax effort to track the smuggling of US chips to China.

For Nvidia, the scandal will significantly reduce its influence over Washington’s technology policy. Most tech companies have big lobbying outfits, but Nvidia’s approach to policy advocacy was uniquely confrontational. Many chip companies argued that their products should be allowed into China on mundane commercial grounds. But Huang attacked the premise of Washington’s controls, describing China hawks as shameful.

The company’s general counsel, Tim Teter, is even reported to have reached out to the commerce department regarding investigations into Megaspeed, the company where alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang was an executive.

This sharp-elbowed approach made many enemies. The Republican Party is usually pro-business, but Nvidia’s tactics angered senior legislators. Brian Mast, the Republican chair of the House of Representatives foreign affairs committee, attacked Huang earlier this year on social media for “fighting to sell millions of advanced AI chips to Chinese military companies”. Republican Senator Jim Banks has spent the past year working with leftwing Democrat Elizabeth Warren to pass legislation restricting AI chip sales. Nvidia has only itself to blame for a long list of adversaries on both sides of Congress.

Huang’s most powerful friend — the US president — was already weakened by defeat in the midterm elections. He will be weakened further by investigations into his relationship with Nvidia.

One question is what he knew and when. The FT has reported that the president was briefed in May on Huang’s relationship with the alleged Chinese agent yet took no action. A second question is why his administration continued to allow chip sales to Megaspeed throughout this period.

More broadly, Congress is frustrated that the Trump administration came to office promising tough restrictions yet has not delivered. Even before the current scandal broke, Congress was advancing legislation to force tighter controls.

The MATCH Act would force the administration to tighten controls on chipmaking equipment. The AI Overwatch Act would do the same for AI chips. The Chip Security Act would mandate deployment of technologies to track chips’ location. Now these bills are more likely to pass, perhaps as part of a defence spending package later this year.

Pressure is also rising to restrict Chinese access to data centres abroad. One nuance of US chip controls was that, while Chinese companies are not allowed to buy high-end AI chips or bring them into the country, they can rent access in overseas data centres. This is what Megaspeed did on behalf of Alibaba. Nvidia argued that companies like Megaspeed, largely based in south-east Asia, were normal customers. The revelation that it was linked to a suspected Chinese agent makes the argument harder to sustain.

In addition to passing new restrictions, Congress will probably continue investigating Nvidia’s senior leadership. For example, what did other leaders know about Megaspeed? Did the company attempt to intervene in an investigation into Megaspeed, rather than establishing an effective compliance programme? When the new Democratic-led Congress is seated in January, Nvidia’s $25mn donation to Trump’s ballroom will become a liability rather than an asset.

For Nvidia and its investors, the irony is that the China market was small. The scale of smuggling is uncertain, but research from the Institute for Progress suggests it would not account for a large fraction of Nvidia’s revenue. It does not compare to the cost of the chaos that this scandal has caused.

Nvidia needs a path forward in the post-Jensen era. It must reshuffle its senior leadership, reset its relationship with Washington and recognise that even America’s most valuable company cannot dictate the country’s foreign policy. Huang spent the past few years angering Washington by calling its China policy misguided. If anyone was misguided in their dealings with China, it was him.
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】英伟达(Nvidia)董事会、首席执行官黄仁勋(Jensen Huang)在美国半导体政策与全球供应链环境：推动领导层继任规划、重塑对美政策游说与沟通机制
【起因与机理】地缘政治博弈加剧，半导体产业政策已从商业逻辑转向国家安全主导
【关键技术规格】管理层换代压力与组织架构调整紧迫性。
【各方立场与态度】技术领先性与国家安全政策的博弈失衡。
fact_bullets_en: [Core Event] Nvidia Board of Directors, CEO Jensen Huang: Initiating leadership succession and restructuring D.C. lobbying efforts
[Root Cause & Mechanism] Geopolitical rivalry causing a shift from commercial logic to state-directed security mandates
[Key Fact Detail] Urgency for leadership transition and organizational restructuring.
[Key Position & Outlook] The friction between technological hegemony and national security mandates.

news.title: How Jensen Huang built a multibillion-dollar business to let Chinese companies access Nvidia AI chips in SE Asian data centers, exploiting a gap in US sanctions (Wall Street Journal)

news.author: Wall Street Journal
news.content_snippet: Massive data centers in Southeast Asia exploited a gap in U.S. sanctions, providing crucial computing power for Chinese companies and a cover for alleged chip smuggling
news.summary_en: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has established a high-performance computing network in Southeast Asian nations, including Singapore, Malaysia, and Indonesia, providing Chinese firms access to advanced AI chips via cloud-based leasing. This strategy exploits current U.S. export control loopholes by shifting from physical hardware delivery to cross-border compute resource consumption.
news.article_content_en:
Jensen Huang and Nvidia have propelled the AI boom that has lifted the stock market and driven data center construction.

It took more than 30 years for Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang to grow his start-up from a minnow of the video game industry to one of the world’s most valuable companies.

His signature leather jacket, frequent media appearances and close relationship with President Donald Trump made Huang one of the most iconic CEOs of the artificial intelligence era, providing computer chips and financing that have helped sustain an economic boom that has lifted millions of investment and retirement accounts. He helped reshape U.S. policy toward China.

Two major Nvidia shareholders are calling on the board of directors to weigh all options for the company's future leadership, including "the potential return of Jensen Huang."

Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner posted a letter on X on Friday that urges Nvidia's board to "pursue a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia." The letter is also signed by Atreides Management's Gavin Baker.

Nvidia was Altimeter Capital's largest disclosed equity holding in it
news.summary_en: Brad Gerstner of Altimeter Capital and Gavin Baker of Atreides Management have urged Nvidia's board to avoid rushed leadership succession following Jensen Huang's resignation. Huang stepped down amid personal misconduct allegations and federal investigations into Megaspeed, a client currently under DOJ scrutiny for potential illicit diversion of AI chips to China, with interim CEO Colette Kress currently leading operations.

news.title: Sean Duffy blames Friday's FAA outage on copper-to-fiber wiring work at a remote facility, saying contractor L3Harris may have installed a "faulty router" (Joseph Pisani/Wall Street Journal)
news.title_en: Sean Duffy blames Friday's FAA outage on copper-to-fiber wiring work at a remote facility, saying contractor L3Harris may have installed a "faulty router" (Joseph Pisani/Wall Street Journal)
news.author: Wall Street Journal
news.content_snippet: Work at a single remote location caused instability that led authorities to order nationwide groundstop; airlines continue to cancel flights as they rush to reset
news.summary_en: FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford and officials identified that the nationwide flight ground stop was caused by maintenance work upgrading copper wiring to fiber at a remote facility. The investigation currently focuses on whether long-time contractor L3Harris installed a faulty router or committed installation errors, which triggered a network flood within the air traffic control system.
news.article_content_en:
L3Harris, a long time contractor for the Federal Aviation Administration, was doing routine maintenance in at least one of FAA's remote locations changing copper wire to fiber, he said. Duffy said the routers in these facilities were manufactured in 2001. These updates have been happening in American institutions for decades, Duffy said.

"Virtually every single institution in America has gone from copper to fiber, from analog to digital," Duffy said. "Just maybe the FAA is the last one to be doing this work because the investments haven't been made, but this is not complicated."

L3Harris did not immediately respond to NPR's request for comment.

Duffy said the FAA is still investigating the exact error that started flooding other routers in the air traffic control system.

"It's pretty straightforward work that we were doing yesterday at, again, a very remote location. So what we're working to determine was whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error, installator error from L3Harris, or did they install a faulty router?"

Bryan Bedford, the FAA administrator, who joined Duffy at the briefing said there was no evidence of anything nefarious happening or AI-related issues.

Tens of thousands of passengers across the U.S. are still stranded Saturday after a rare ground stop halted all flights.

The chaos is expected to linger for days.

The aviation system is back online and slowly returning to normal Saturday morning, but delays and cancellations will continue after yesterday's nationwide ground stop, Duffy said in the press briefing Saturday.

"Based on everything that we're hearing from our airline partners, they believe that they'll be able to have full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday," Bedford said.

Duffy told reporters Friday night: "I think we're going to be back up and operational as we come into the heat of travel during Thanksgiving."

For about four hours on Friday, thousands of flights at U.S. airports were grounded in one of the biggest disruptions of the nation's air travel system since the terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001.

Nearly 25,000 flights were delayed, and over 9,000 were cancelled on Friday, according to FlightAware, a flight tracking site. The disruption seeped into Saturday morning with more than 4,000 cancellations recorded. That's 14% of flights departing the U.S., according to data from Cirium, which tracks aviation analytics.

Duffy said Friday that air traffic control facilities had experienced "intermittent" outages of their radar and communications systems beginning earlier in the afternoon. Duffy blamed "old switches, old routers" for the failures. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin joined Duffy in the White House briefing room and said there was no evidence the issue was due to an attack.

Flight boards at airports across the country Saturday morning continued to be riddled with red cancelled marks. At Tampa International Airport in Florida, people in the main terminal area before security curled up in chairs to grab a wink of sleep.

On Friday night, a flight board at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport in D.C. showed dozens of flights delayed into the early morning hours or cancelled.

Passengers Erin and Jake Britt spent half the day at the airport in D.C. on Friday. Their plane to Fort Lauderdale, Fla. boarded at 3 p.m. By 5:30 p.m., they were getting off the plane — but they were still in D.C.

"Overall, our plane was definitely annoyed, but reasonable," Erin Britt said, as the couple left the airport at 8pm. "People being upset and asking like, 'Well, how are you not prepared for this?' And it was like, 'Well, no one was prepared.'"

She said neither the pilot nor flight attendants had any more information than passengers."They seem just as in the dark," she said.

The pair decided to cancel their weekend trip, but the night didn't end there. They spent over nine hours overnight waiting on the JetBlue customer service call line to be reimbursed. "I was setting alarms in 20 minute intervals in case I fell asleep," Erin Britt said.

For people who had events or plans over the weekend – the delay added an extra layer of stress. Joe Romano and Maddie Cabana had a cruise leaving Orlando, Fla. Saturday afternoon.

"It was a big eye roll. I mean, I travel a lot for work already, so I'm constantly dealing with flight delays," Romano said. "When this happened, I was just like, 'Of course, it always happens to me.'"

"Just rather inconvenient and frustrating," Cabana added, as the pair contemplated checking their bags or going home. "Hopefully, everything will be fine. It'll all work out. It always does."

And it did – eventually. After their JetBlue flight was ultimately cancelled, they quickly booked another one on Southwest Airlines and made it early Saturday morning.

"My husband, my hero, is driving down from New Jersey to come get me," DiPietro said.

Other alternatives included people switching to Amtrak trains as they struggled to get to their destination. Although, even Amtrak's system had a brief outage Friday night.

This was only the second nationwide ground stop since September 11, 2001. The U.S. last issued a ground stop of this scale in 2023, when all U.S. airports were shut down due to an outage in the NOTAM (Notice to Air Missions) system, which alerts pilots and airports of real-time hazards.

That outage prompted fears of a cyberattack, but the FAA later determined the issue was caused when contract workers inadvertently deleted critical files.

The FAA has recently begun rolling out an AI-enhanced software tool known as the SMART system as part of its ambitious overhaul of the nation's air traffic control system. But Air Space Intelligence, the company that makes the tool, quickly dismissed speculation that its product could be connected to the flight disruptions.

"The current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC," the company said on social media.

news.title: Sean Duffy blames Friday's FAA outage on copper-to-fiber wiring work at a remote facility, saying contractor L3Harris may have installed a "faulty router" (Joseph Pisani/Wall Street Journal)
news.title_en: Sean Duffy blames Friday's FAA outage on copper-to-fiber wiring work at a remote facility, saying contractor L3Harris may have installed a "faulty router" (Joseph Pisani/Wall Street Journal)
news.author: Wall Street Journal
news.content_snippet: Work at a single remote location caused instability that led authorities to order nationwide groundstop; airlines continue to cancel flights as they rush to reset
news.summary_en: US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed that Friday's massive flight grounding was caused by a router malfunction at an FAA remote facility during a copper-to-fiber upgrade project by contractor L3Harris. The device flooded communication networks with excess connection attempts, disrupting radar and aircraft links, though systems have since been isolated and restored.
news.article_content_en:
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Saturday that air traffic operations had fully resumed after a telecommunications problem disrupted flights Friday, prompting a ground stop while about 3,500 aircraft were airborne.At a news conference, Duffy said preliminary findings pointed to work at a remote Federal Aviation Administration location, where contractor L3Harris was replacing aging copper telecommunications lines with fiber.A router involved in that work began flooding other routers with more than 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, disrupting communications with aircraft and some radar feeds, Duffy said.Officials were still determining whether the problem stemmed from a faulty router or an installation error.

Duffy said authorities did not believe a cyberattack was responsible."Once we were able to isolate the work that was being done at this remote location, all of our systems came back online," he said.In a statement Saturday, L3Harris explained that it has been working in close coordination with the FAA on the conversion from legacy copper wires to a fiber optic system, and indicated the project is 70% completed.

"We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the Nov. 13 ground stop of our nation’s air travel," the statement continued.Duffy credited air traffic controllers and pilots with safely landing the aircraft and thanked passengers for their patience during the disruption.He also urged Congress to provide additional funding to modernize the air traffic control system.

Duffy said the FAA has replaced 69% of its copper communications with high-speed fiber as part of upgrades supported by $12.5 billion Congress provided."Americans want less delays. They want less cancellations," Duffy said.More than 2,500 flights were canceled in the U.S. on Saturday and hundreds more were delayed, according to FlightAware, a website that tracks flight disruptions.That’s on top of more than 9,000 canceled flights and 7,000 delayed flights on Friday.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said the air travel schedule should be back to normal by the end of Sunday. He said airlines "will still have delays and cancellations" Saturday but assured the "worst is behind us."Airlines are obligated to offer free rebooking on another flight for travelers who want to continue their journey, or a refund if their flight was canceled and they decide not to take the trip.Delta and United announced they were offering travel waivers.

MORE: Airlines issue travel waivers during national ground stopPassengers should contact their airlines for information about their flights and any potential compensation, the FAA said. A new rule that went into effect last month could make it harder for airline customers to get compensated.

Effective Oct. 19, the Department of Transportation removed 10 events from being considered "within an airline's control," removing the ability for flyers to be compensated. RELATED: Nationwide ground stop: How new DOT rule could affect compensation for flight delaysAmong the 10 events are "government system failures," or unexpected shutdowns or technical failures of government systems that directly impact safe flight operations.Duffy suggested more disruptions might occur in coming days, but officials say the system is likely to be operating normally in time to handle the Thanksgiving travel rush.

news.title_en: Gemini 4 Carbon takes the MathArena crown but costs 15 times more than GPT-6.1 Sol
news.author: THE DECODER
news.content_snippet:
Google's Gemini 4 Carbon has become the first non-OpenAI model in a while to top the MathArena math benchmark. It knocked GPT-6.1 Sol from the top spot, while Claude Fable 5.2 came in second, making it potentially one of the most capable publicly available models for math tasks. OpenAI's models, which recently allegedly solved demanding equations like the Navier-Stokes equations, aren't publicly available yet.

Gemini 4 Carbon's most common failure mode is exceeding the time limit. The model als
news.summary_en: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon model surpassed OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol to top the MathArena math benchmark, with Claude Fable 5.2 ranking second. news.title: Trump Media faces a Nov. 30 deadline to repay up to $1B in convertible bonds sold last May to fund a "bitcoin treasury," as its shares are down 60+% this year (Financial Times)
news.title_en: Trump Media faces a Nov. 30 deadline to repay up to $1B in convertible bonds sold last May to fund a "bitcoin treasury," as its shares are down 60+% this year (Financial Times)
news.author: Financial Times
news.content_snippet: Plunge in shares and cryptocurrency prices could force Truth Social owner to sell assets or take on costly new debt
news.summary_en: Trump Media & Technology Group (NASDAQ: DJT) faces a critical liquidity event as creditors may demand the repayment of up to $1 billion in convertible notes by November 30. On-chain data indicates the transfer of 4,259 BTC in collateral to Crypto.com, highlighting acute financial stress amidst a year-to-date share price decline of over 60% and $1.8 billion in cumulative losses.
news.article_content_en:
The Crypto Desk desk. Editor: Sam Daodu.

This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Wallets linked to Trump Media (NASDAQ: DJT), labeled as “2028 Convertible Notes Collateral,” transferred 4,259 Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) to Crypto.com, according to Arkham data. While no sale has been confirmed, blockchain data shows the coins’ movement without clarifying whether they were sold. These Bitcoins are tied to a debt, and creditors can demand repayment of about $1 billion by November 30.

Arkham tracked the transfer of the coins in two batches, 2,140.03 BTC and 2,119.31 BTC, logged within an hour on that day. Subsequently, Whale Alert reported that 4,259 BTC left Crypto.com for an unidentified wallet. Crypto.com operates both an exchange and custody service, so the coins might be headed for either a trading desk or a secure vault.

At present, Bitcoin trades at $76,517, down 4.8% over the last 24 hours, back below $80,000 after closing above that level on November 4. Trump Media shares are trading at $4.54, up 1% but down 24% over the past week.

Convertible notes are essentially loans that can be converted into company stock at a later date. Trump Media has pledged Bitcoin as collateral for its 2028 convertible notes. This means that if the company fails to repay its lenders, those lenders can claim the Bitcoin. The number of Bitcoins transferred aligns with the amount pledged as collateral in a recent quarterly report.

Although the notes mature in 2028, holders can demand repayment of about $1 billion on November 30. This looming deadline has raised eyebrows, especially after the recent collateral transfer.

Despite reporting a surge in revenue, with Trump Media generating $1.7 million in the second quarter—an 89% year-over-year increase—this amount pales in comparison to its $1.9 billion in financial assets. Non-cash losses during the same quarter hit $190.4 million due to unliquidated holdings.

Market analyst Charlie Bilello pointed out that Trump Media’s stock has plummeted 97% from its peak, reaching another all-time low. With cumulative losses of $1.8 billion since its inception, shares have dropped by 11% following the Democrats’ control of Congress, putting DJT down 66% for the year.

The company is also pursuing a merger with TAE Technologies, expected to close in the fourth quarter. Both the merger and the impending repayment deadline will be significant factors for management as the year wraps up.

Trump Media has not publicly addressed the Bitcoin transfers, nor has it filed any new Form 8-K with the SEC to report significant developments. Without a named buyer, sale price, or counterparty, the purpose of the Bitcoin transfer remains uncertain.

Whale Alert’s information further complicates matters because it cannot distinguish whether the transfer was an over-the-counter sale, a custody transfer, or an internal wallet shuffle. While deposits to exchanges often precede sales, the trail lacks clarity at this unknown address.

With Bitcoin priced at $76,517, the 4,259 BTC are valued at about $326 million. However, even if the Bitcoin were sold, the amount wouldn’t fully cover the $1 billion debt if all lenders requested cash.

While a 4,259 BTC transaction is significant for one wallet, it represents only a small fraction of the overall market. On November 4, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs took in a net $74.6 million, ending a three-day streak that pulled $1.3 billion from Bitcoin and Ethereum funds. Trump Media’s Bitcoin represents 4.4 times the amount brought into the ETFs that day.

This 4,259 BTC transfer signifies about 0.02% of Bitcoin’s circulating supply of roughly 20.1 million coins. Although a sale could momentarily affect the price, it remains a minor part of the total market. The name “Trump” also appears in connection with American Bitcoin (NASDAQ: ABTC), a distinct mining company that reported net income of about $126 million in the third quarter, although this data pertains to a different entity.

While no definitive sale has occurred, the transfer does not confirm one either. Moving coins from a collateral wallet to an exchange, then to an unknown address, could indicate a sale, a custody shift, or an arrangement with lenders—but without more information from Trump Media, the narrative remains open-ended.

Regardless of the path Trump Media chooses, a sale or transfer to lenders could help reduce its debt, while repayment in cash would let the company keep the Bitcoin on its books. For Bitcoin, the implications are minimal, as a corporate debt decision wouldn’t create new buyers, and a sale would only add to the supply.

A sale of 4,259 BTC seems unlikely to crash Bitcoin’s price, since it accounts for only about 0.02% of the total supply. Bitcoin’s broader issue lies in the ongoing trend of its value, as it currently trades 39.3% below its all-time high of $126,080. It remains below its 20-day and 50-day moving averages but stays above its 200-day average.

Contact [email protected] for any questions or corrections.

Sam Daodu is a crypto analyst and the editor of 24/7 Wall St.'s Crypto Desk, where he covers Bitcoin, XRP, Ethereum, Solana and the altcoins investors search for most. His work focuses on price levels, spot ETF flows, on-chain data and the regulatory decisions that move crypto markets, written so a first-time buyer and a seasoned trader can both use it. Sam has written about crypto professionally since 2019 and has published more than 2,000 articles. Before joining 24/7 Wall St., he wrote for crypto media outlets and Web3 companies and ghostwrote for crypto founders and token launches. His analysis is syndicated on Yahoo Finance, MSN and AOL and has been cited by other crypto news sites. He also founded MacLabs Marketing, a content and personal branding agency for crypto founders and executives. When he isn't reading charts, Sam is usually at the gym or watching One Piece, a series he maintains has better tokenomics than most altcoins.

one of the more interesting developments in the ai agent economy is agents hiring other agents to get work done.

@termix_ai recently showcased this through Montage Studio on https://t.co/9ReKMK2L7m.

here's how it works.

you submit a video production brief. Montage Studio breaks it into smaller jobs and hires specialized agents to handle the storyboard, video rendering and music.

it then coordinates their work, combines the results and delivers the finished video.

each job goes through escrow on TermiX.

this shows how agents can take responsibility for larger tasks, outsource specialized work and pay other agents for their contributions.

but this requires more than communication. agents need to discover services, agree on prices, secure payments, verify delivery and handle disputes.

that's where TermiX's Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol (AACP) comes in.

its workflow brings the process together:

escrow → delivery → challenge → settlement.

with TermiX Skills, agents can also connect to the marketplace, find work and participate in these transactions.

the direction is clear: agents are moving beyond isolated tasks towards hiring, coordinating and paying other agents to complete larger jobs.

that's the kind of autonomous economy TermiX is building towards.

when agents start doing business with each other, reliable transaction infrastructure becomes essential.

#TermiX #AACP

telling an AI agent what it shouldn't do is different from making it technically unable to do it.

when an AI agent is handling someone's money, that difference matters.

you can tell an agent to avoid certain assets, set a spending limit or stop trading after a certain loss. but if it still has broad permission to execute transactions, those instructions only go so far.

with MOTES (@meetmotes), the owner sets the mandate and signs the permissions. before a proposed transaction goes through, the smart account checks it against the rules the owner approved.

so the agent can still analyse the market and come up with strategies, but it has to work within those limits. it can't just give itself permission to spend more or trade assets outside the approved list.

i think this is a better foundation for autonomous finance. giving an agent the ability to make decisions is one thing. making sure it only has the authority the owner gave it is just as important.

A user discovered a hidden chip in an off-brand power bank purchased in Guangzhou using Claude Code.

Every time it charged an iPhone, it secretly copied the entire phone's data. It also read Wi-Fi passwords, connected to the home network, and sent all the information to a remote server.

This power bank was bought at the airport three weeks ago for $19, labeled as 30,000 mAh, hefty with no brand name.

When first plugged in, the screen prompted "Trust This Computer," and the user clicked trust without thinking, granting it one-click access to read all data.

This morning, after setting up Claude Code to monitor file reads, the screen flashed yellow and red warnings just 10 seconds into charging—data was being transmitted.

The power bank was identified as a mini-computer with built-in 64 GB storage and network connectivity.

Regular charging cables only use power lines, but this one uses both power and data lines, and it has already copied:

→ Device info, 1,206 contacts
→ All apps including 2 banking apps
→ 3,912 photos including passport
→ Wi-Fi network names and keys
→ Wife's iPhone photos

Every charge, it uses the key to go online and send new data—19 uploads over 3 weeks, last one at 2:14 AM last night.

The user immediately unplugged it, used Claude Code to block that IP, and changed the Wi-Fi password and banking app logins.

A repair shop took it apart for a look—details below. Suggestion: Check every power bank in your home today.

celebrity.full_text_en:
China cracked recursive self-improvement 🤯

Tencent dropped 27B model that rewrites, retrains, and refines itself.. with zero human in the loop.

It’s called "Terminal-RSI" and it solves one of the biggest problems with AI.

They are incredibly lazy.

Usually, an agent will make partial progress, claim it succeeded, and completely fail the final environment verifier check. this new pipeline forces agents to actually finish the job.

here’s how it works:

they built a recursive loop with two alternating phases..

- RSR (recursive self-rewrite): the model fine-tunes itself on its own successfully rewritten trajectories

- RPR (recursive policy-refine): it then runs reinforcement learning (ppo) using a "critic" inherited directly from the previous stage to lock in those discovered behaviors

- Loop: the training sequence leapfrogs itself: Base → RSR-1 → RPR-1 → RSR-2 → RPR-2

and the numbers are insane..

they applied this to a qwen3.8-27b base model. across the four "terminal-bench" suites, the agent's average success rate jumped from 20.68% all the way to 50.58%.

on the absolute hardest benchmark suite (terminal-bench 4.0), the base model scored a flat 0.00%.

after terminal-rsi?

it hit 19.84% (putting it right on par with reference models like gemini 3.8 flash).

the secret sauce? they fixed the reward system.

instead of giving the ai "dense rewards" for just trying or passing semantic checks, they switched to a "success-prioritized reward" (spr).

it mathematically separates strict success from partial credit.

basically, the agent only gets the massive reward payout if the code actually passes the final terminal gate.. so it stops faking success.

the gap between partial local repairs and strict terminal verification is closing fast.

we are watching agents build their own training environments and level up autonomously.. the future is wild.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
中国破解了递归自我完善🤯

腾讯放弃了重写、重新训练和完善自身的 27B 模型……循环中零人力。

它被称为“Terminal-RSI”，它解决了人工智能最大的问题之一。

他们非常懒惰。

通常，代理会取得部分进展，声称已成功，但最终环境验证程序检查完全失败。这条新管道迫使特工真正完成工作。

它的工作原理如下：

他们建立了一个具有两个交替阶段的递归循环。

- RSR（递归自重写）：模型根据自己成功重写的轨迹进行自我微调

- RPR（递归策略细化）：然后使用直接从前一阶段继承的“批评家”来运行强化学习（ppo），以锁定那些发现的行为

- 循环：训练序列自行跳跃：Base → RSR-1 → RPR-1 → RSR-2 → RPR-2

而且数字很疯狂..

他们将其应用于 qwen3.8-27b 基础模型。在四个“终端替补”套件中，特工的平均成功率从 20.68% 一路跃升至 50.58%。

在绝对最难的基准测试套件（terminal-bench 4.0）上，基本模型的得分为 0.00%。

在终端 rsi 之后？

它达到了 19.84%（与 Gemini 3.8 flash 等参考型号相当）。

秘密武器？他们确定了奖励制度。

他们不再为人工智能尝试或通过语义检查而给予“密集奖励”，而是转向“成功优先奖励”（spr）。

它在数学上将严格的成功与部分的功劳区分开来。

基本上，只有当代码实际上通过了最终的终端门时，代理才会获得巨额奖励。因此它不再假装成功。

部分本地修复和严格的终端验证之间的差距正在迅速缩小。

我们正在观察代理建立自己的培训环境并自主升级......未来是疯狂的。

基本上，只有当代码实际上通过了最终的终端门时，代理才会获得巨额奖励。因此它不再假装成功。

部分本地修复和严格的终端验证之间的差距正在迅速缩小。

我们正在观察代理建立自己的培训环境并自主升级......未来是疯狂的。

celebrity.full_text_en:
i killed the infographics show with 1 claude opus prompt

now i made a full 10 minute story video in full code

this cost me $0 in ai video generations btw

turned it into a prompt you can use for free and make any topic u want, enjoy ↓

<inputs>
Ask me for my topic and my script. If I have no script, write one from my topic.
Ask which image model I have: GPT Image 2, or any model that takes reference images at 2K-4K, at about $0.03-0.05 an image.
Ask which voice I have: ElevenLabs, or Kokoro for free.
Before generating everything, show me a look test: one plate, one character sheet cut out and rigged, and a 10 s shot with typing, a tag and a character who talks and points. Wait for my OK.
</inputs>

<look>
A 1920x1080 animated explainer in the style of the big flat-vector infographic channels.
- Every line of narration is acted out by cartoon people inside a full illustrated place.
- All motion is code. There are no AI video generations, just a few still images that code cuts up, rigs and animates.

Art:
- Flat colour shapes with NO outlines, at most one slightly darker flat shade for form, simple geometric shapes and crisp edges.
- Muted palette: dusty blue-grey, slate teal, warm beige, navy, soft purple. Salmon-pink skin, big round heads, dot eyes, small bodies.
- Mood comes from the plate's own light: daylight, a cold blue night, warm indoor lamps.

Code colours:
- ink #2b2d42, red #d62828, orange #f4a261, gold #f6b93b, green #2fb37a, navy #1f2a48
- headline tomato #e2552f and purple #5b3fa6
- grey labels #8a8c9c, white cards #ffffff
- Font: Montserrat 800-900 (Google Fonts), all caps on cards and signs.

Pace:
- A new place every 3-4 s, about 10 places a minute.
- Something new arrives every 2 s: a tag, a stamp, a person walking in, a number.
- Never hold a still over 1 s. Never have a character who doesn't move.

Banned:
- outlines, glossy UI panels floating over the art, emoji, burned-in subtitles
- any channel's logo or name, photos of real people
- facts written on a plain colour card when the place could hold them
</look>

<art>
About 60 images in all ($2-3).

Every prompt starts with this style core, word for word:
"Flat vector illustration in exactly the same art style as the reference images: NO outlines or line art anywhere, every shape is a flat solid colour fill with at most one slightly darker flat shade for form, simple geometric shapes, crisp clean edges, no gradients, no texture, no painterly lighting. Muted modern palette: dusty blue-grey, slate teal, warm beige, navy, soft purple, salmon-pink skin. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos."

Then add one line that locks the setting ("The setting is [time, place]: [materials, light sources], nothing from other eras unless asked"). Feed 3-5 frames of a reference channel in as style references, with their logo cropped off.

1. Hero plates, about 24, one full 16:9 image each, for places you zoom into or come back to.
   - EMPTY: "no people, no characters, no animals".
   - Straight-on, with an open floor in the middle where characters will stand.
   - Blank signs, boards, screens and pages that code writes on later.
2. Quad plates, about 19, giving 76 more places. Pack 4 places into one image:
   "The image is a 2x2 grid of FOUR completely separate scenes, each filling exactly one quarter of the image (each quarter is itself a 16:9 picture), divided by perfectly straight thin pure-white gutters, one vertical down the exact centre and one horizontal across the exact centre."
   - Then describe the TOP-LEFT, TOP-RIGHT, BOTTOM-LEFT and BOTTOM-RIGHT scenes.
   - Split each quad on the brightest white row and column near the centre, walk out while the line stays over 60% white, and trim 6 px more.
   - Crop each tile to 16:9 at 1920x1080.
   - Object close-ups make great tiles: a desk, a screen, a document, a plate of food, a vault.
3. Main characters, 2-3 of them. Write one fixed description per character (age, hair, face, every piece of clothing with colours) and paste it word for word into every sheet.
   - Base sheet: 6 views. (1) front, neutral, drawn WITHOUT ARMS, only round smooth shoulder sockets where the arms would join; (2) the same armless front with a second emotion; (3) side view walking right; (4) seen from behind; (5) and (6) two poses the script needs.
   - Expression sheet: 6 armless fronts (hopeful, disgusted, terrified, exhausted, sick, shocked, or whatever the script needs), with the base sheet as a reference.
   - Pose sheet: 6 full poses with their props (sitting at a desk typing, sleeping, eating, running, signing, falling), with the base sheet as a reference.
4. Everyone else: role sheets of 4-6 people, each drawn in the exact pose their shot needs; crowd sheets of 8-10 small figures; prop sheets.
   - Every sheet: "on a solid flat chroma green background (#00B140) with lots of empty green space between figures; nothing touches, nothing on any character or object is green, full bodies, nothing cut off by the edges".
5. Thumbnail art: the same characters with richer saturated cartoon lighting and extreme emotions, the top quarter left free, no text, with the base sheets as references.
</art>

<rig>
Cutouts:
- The background is every border-connected pixel with G - max(R,B) over 40 and within 110 of the median green. Key only from the border, or dark clothes leak.
- Add a 2 px soft alpha band and clamp G to max(R,B) + 6 inside it, which kills the green fringe.
- Group the pieces by figure and drop specks. Name every sprite, and show me a named contact sheet.

Armless front figures become puppets:
- Split the head at the neck: the narrowest alpha row under the head.
- Find both shoulder sockets and the eye boxes.
- Inpaint the hole under the head from the body's own colours, so a nod never shows a gap.
- Write everything to rig.js: size, neck, sockets, eye boxes, skin RGB, sleeve RGB.
- Arms: upper L1 about 0.13 of the figure's height, lower L2 about 0.12, thickness about 0.04. Use sleeve colour to the elbow and skin for the forearm, a 0.82x darker sleeve when the arm is behind the body, and round caps and joins.
- Hands: mittens in three shapes (mitt, open, fist), plus a point with one finger out.
- Arm poses: each is a hand target relative to its shoulder, in units of L = L1 + L2, solved by two-bone IK (where there are two signs, the first is the left arm).
  - down: (∓0.04, 0.97)
  - rest: (±0.1, 0.9)
  - hips: (∓0.42, 0.55) with fists
  - point: right hand to (0.86, -0.32)
  - present: right hand to (0.75, 0.25), open
  - shrug: (∓0.62, 0.12), open
  - up: (∓0.32, -0.9)
  - hands on head
  - chin: a fist at the neck
  - hold: (±0.42, 0.45)
  - wave: (0.5, -0.75)
  - stop: (0.55, -0.1)
  - cheer: (∓0.55, -0.75) with fists
  - A pose change blends the two targets over 0.3-0.5 s with ease-in-out.
- Side, back and pose sprites stay whole images. Only the head turns, and a drawing or typing hand jitters ±6 px.
</rig>

<animation>
One HTML canvas where every frame is a pure function of time t: window .seek(t), READY, END, and EV, a list of sound events by name.
- Hang every shot on the narration: S('exact words', fn) starts a shot 0.08 s before that phrase. Repeated words are looked up by occurrence number.
- One function per shot, one shots file per chapter.

Motion primitives (Δ = t - start):
- pop: 0.3 s back-ease overshoot, 1 + 2.9(p-1)^3 + 1.9(p-1)^2.
- spring in: 1 - e^(-6.5Δ) cos(13Δ).
- kick on impact: 1 + 0.1 e^(-10Δ) cos(22Δ).
- shake: x = A e^(-8Δ) sin(61Δ), y = A e^(-8Δ) cos(47Δ).
- Exits shrink with ease-in over 0.25 s. Things arrive with a spring, a squash or a white puff, never a plain fade.

Camera:
- camP(plate, zoom, fx, fy) keeps the view inside the plate's edges.
- Every shot moves from one [zoom, fx, fy] to another with ease-in-out, a 2-4% push or a slow pan, so nothing holds still.
- Draw the plate and everything on it inside the same camera transform.
- Keep zoom under 1.33x on quad tiles. Zoom deeper only on hero plates.

Transitions:
- Push: the old shot slides out left while the new one slides in from the right, 0.24 s ease-in-out, with a whoosh 0.02 s before.
- Chapter splat: a #f4f1fb blob covers the screen in 0.2 s and clears in 0.2 s. It's a 1,250 px circle, 12 big satellite blobs at golden-angle spacing and 10 small droplets further out, shifted 120 px left on the way in and 140 px right on the way out.

Characters, alive in every frame:
- Breathing: scale 1 + 0.009 sin(2.3t).
- Head nod: 0.025 sin(2.1t) rad, or 0.025 sin(7t) + 0.02 sin(11.3t) while that character's line is spoken.
- Blink: every 2.7-4.2 s, seeded per figure. For 0.14 s, paint each eye box over in skin colour with a curved lash line.
- Walk:
  - Bob |sin| at 2.2% of the figure's height, with a body rock of ±0.035 rad.
  - Side-view walk sprites slide 1.5 leg lengths per step cycle, so the feet don't skate.
- Enter on the spring, sometimes with a hop. Fear is a fast shake (sin 70t). Surprise is a jump and an orange "!".
- A soft contact shadow ellipse under every figure. Night shots darken them with brightness(1 - k), so they match the plate.
- Every character on screen acts on its line: points at the thing being named, presents it, shrugs, cheers, holds its head.
</animation>

<graphics>
Text only lives on things in the world, typed letter by letter: 28 letters a second (34 for short tags). Each letter starts 1.45x big and 0.7 em to the right and settles in 0.18 s with ease-out.

The full kit:
- Board: a white rounded board (radius 20) that drops 420 px on the spring and swings 0.25 rad into place, or stands on a wooden post and swings up from -1 rad.
  - Soft drop shadow (blur 22, y 8, 22%) and a faint darker strip along its bottom edge.
  - Lines typed 0.3 s apart.
- Date card: top left at (70, 70), white, 120 px tall, at least 330 px wide, radius 18. An orange calendar icon, a grey "DATE:" at 26 px, the date typed at 44 px weight 900. Pops in over 0.32 s.
- Place card: the same card with a red map pin and "PLACE:".
- Tag: a 6 px line with a dot at the thing, drawn in 0.2 s, then a rounded pill (the text at 40 px weight 900) pops on its end. Ink, red, gold or orange pills.
- Number card: a white card with a small grey label and a big red number. Long numbers roll up like a counter with ease-out.
- Red X: two round 30 px strokes, 0.11 s each, 0.01 s apart, with a soft shadow. One goes over every wrong idea.
- Stamp: red text in a double rounded border, tilted -0.12 rad. It slams from 2.1x to 1x in 0.14 s, then kicks.
- Banner: a full-width headline band, 92 px white caps on tomato or purple, rotated -0.02 rad, sliding in from the left over 0.22 s.
- Speech bubble: white, radius 36, with a tail. Thought cloud: a pill with two small circles.
- Orange "?" that bobs and sways over a puzzled head, and an orange "!" pop.
- White puff and poof clouds, speed lines, light blue sweat drops, coins and bills, a soft vignette, and a colour tint for mood.
- Write on the plate's own blank boards, screens and pages whenever the place has them. Measure the blank's rectangle on a grid overlay of the plate first.
</graphics>

<voice>
- ElevenLabs: a deep, warm US documentary narrator, eleven_v4, stability 0.5, similarity 0.75, style 0, speaker boost, with the timestamps endpoint.
- About 170-180 words a minute, using the voice's own speed setting (1.0-1.1). Never speed it up with atempo: it sounds chipmunked.
- Long scripts go in 3 chunks split at chapter breaks, passing the previous and next text so the read stays continuous.
- Cut pauses over 0.24 s to 0.16 s, leave 0.5 s at chapter breaks, and add a 0.3 s lead-in.
- Rebuild word times from the alignment into words.js.
- Run faster-whisper over the result and diff it against the script before building the picture.
- Free route: Kokoro, then faster-whisper for the word times.
</voice>

<sound>
- Music: 2-3 free documentary beds from Pixabay, crossfaded over 3 s at big beats.
- Duck the music under the voice (30 ms attack, 0.3 s hold, 0.45 s release) and let it swell back up between chapters.
- SFX from Mixkit, one per event, aligned by their peaks, 6 dB quieter on speech: a typewriter tick on typing, a whoosh on pushes and splats, a pop on tags and cards, a thud on stamps, a hit on every red X, a ding on ticks, plus sounds that fit the scene.
- Gate: during speech the voice sits 15+ dB over music plus SFX (median of 100 ms frames), and the background is louder than the voice in under 1% of frames.
- Two-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS, true peak -1 dB.
</sound>

<build>
1. Tools: Python, Playwright with Chromium or Edge, FFmpeg, faster-whisper, OpenCV, Pillow, numpy. Install what's missing and tell me what you installed.
2. Order:
   - the look test
   - the art in batches, with a contact sheet after each
   - cutouts and rig
   - voice and word times
   - shots, chapter by chapter
3. Check before any full render: a contact sheet per chapter, one frame every 2 s. Fix:
   - empty or overflowing signs
   - text over a face
   - black plate edges
   - feet floating off the floor
   - two shots in a row in the same place
   - any 4 s where nothing new arrives
4. Render at 30 fps, 4 motion-blur subframes over half a frame, frames piped to libx264 CRF 16-18.
   - Split long videos across 4-6 parallel browser pages and join the parts.
   - Scan the result for single-frame jumps and check that each one is a planned cut.
</build>

<gotchas>
- Too few places reads as lazy. One plate held for 30 s with cards over it looks cheap. Budget about 10 new places a minute.
- Some image models ignore "no arms". GPT Image 2 follows it.
- Paste the same character description into every sheet and feed the base sheet back in, or faces and clothes drift.
- Quad tiles are only about 1920 px wide. Pushing past 1.33x looks soft.
- Plates with people already drawn in can't be animated. Ask for EMPTY and check before cutting.
- Text on a card floating over the art looks like a slideshow. Write on the world.
- Long renders crash. Render in parts you can rerun, and back up the shot files before every big patch.
</gotchas>

<start>
Ask me for my topic, my script, my image model and my voice, then make the look test.
</start>

<看>
大型平面矢量信息图表频道风格的 1920x1080 动画讲解器。
- 每一行叙述都由卡通人物在一个充满插图的地方表演。
- 所有的动作都是代码。没有人工智能视频生成，只有一些经过代码切割、装配和动画处理的静态图像。

艺术：
- 没有轮廓的扁平颜色形状，最多一种稍暗的扁平色调，简单的几何形状和清晰的边缘。
- 柔和的调色板：灰蓝灰色、板岩青色、暖米色、海军蓝、柔和的紫色。鲑鱼粉色的皮肤，圆圆的大脑袋，圆点的眼睛，小小的身体。
- 情绪来自于盘子本身的光线：日光、寒冷的蓝色夜晚、温暖的室内灯光。

代码颜色：
- 墨水 #2b2d42、红色 #d62828、橙色 #f4a261、金色 #f6b93b、绿色 #2fb37a、海军蓝 #1f2a48
- 标题番茄#e2552f 和紫色#5b3fa6
- 灰色标签#8a8c9c，白色卡片#ffffff
- 字体：Montserrat 800-900（Google 字体），卡片和标志上全部大写。

步速：
- 每 3-4 秒一个新位置，每分钟大约 10 个位置。
- 每 2 秒就会有新的东西到达：标签、邮票、走进来的人、号码。
- 切勿保持静止超过 1 秒。永远不要有不动的角色。

禁止：
- 轮廓、漂浮在艺术上方的光滑 UI 面板、表情符号、内置字幕
- 任何频道的标志或名称、真人照片
- 当地方可以容纳时，将事实写在普通彩色卡片上
</看>

<艺术>
总共大约 60 张图片（2-3 美元）。

每个提示都以这种风格核心开头，逐字逐句：
“平面矢量插图的艺术风格与参考图像完全相同：任何地方都没有轮廓或线条艺术，每个形状都是平面纯色填充，最多有一个稍暗的平面阴影作为形式，简单的几何形状，清晰干净的边缘，没有渐变，没有纹理，没有绘画照明。柔和的现代调色板：灰蓝色，板岩青色，温暖米色，海军蓝，柔和的紫色，鲑鱼粉红色皮肤。没有文字，没有字母，没有数字，没有徽标。”

然后添加一行来锁定设置（“设置是[时间，地点]：[材料，光源]，除非询问，否则没有其他时代的内容”）。将参考通道的 3-5 帧作为样式参考，并剪掉其徽标。

1. 英雄板块，大约 24 张，每张一张完整的 16:9 图片，用于您放大或返回的地方。
- 空：“没有人，没有人物，没有动物”。
- 直行，中间有一个开放的地板，角色可以站立。
- 稍后在上面写入代码的空白标志、板、屏幕和页面。
2.四块板，大约19个，多出76个位置。将 4 个位置打包到一张图像中：
“该图像是由四个完全独立的场景组成的 2x2 网格，每个场景正好填充图像的四分之一（每个四分之一本身就是一张 16:9 的图片），由完全笔直的纯白色排水沟划分，一个垂直向下，一个水平穿过正中心。”
- 然后描述左上、右上、左下和右下场景。
- 在中心附近最亮的白色行和列上分割每个四边形，在线条保持超过 60% 的白色时走出去，然后再修剪 6 像素。
- 在 1920x1080 下将每个图块裁剪为 16:9。
- 物体特写可以成为很棒的图块：一张桌子、一个屏幕、一份文件、一盘食物、一个金库。
3.主要人物，2-3人。为每个角色写一个固定的描述（年龄、头发、脸、每件衣服的颜色），然后逐字粘贴到每张纸上。
- 基础表：6 次查看。 (1) 正面，中立，没有手臂，只有手臂连接处的圆形光滑肩窝； （2）同样无臂的正面却有第二种情感； (3)右侧行走侧视图； (4) 从后面看； (5)和(6)两个构成脚本需要。
- 表情表：6 个无臂正面（希望、厌恶、恐惧、疲惫、生病、震惊或脚本需要的任何内容），以基础表作为参考。
- 姿势表：6 个带有道具的完整姿势（坐在办公桌前打字、睡觉、吃饭、跑步、签名、摔倒），以基础表作为参考。
4. 其他人：4-6 人的角色表，每个人都按照他们的拍摄需要的准确姿势绘制； 8-10 个小数字的人群表；道具表。
- 每张纸：“在坚实的平坦色度绿色背景上（#00B140），人物之间有很多空白的绿色空间；没有任何接触，任何角色或物体上没有任何东西是绿色的，全身，没有被边缘切断的东西”。
5.缩略图艺术：相同的角色，具有更丰富的饱和卡通灯光和极端的情感，上四分之一留空，没有文字，以底纸为参考。
</艺术>

<装备>
剪纸：
- 背景是 G - max(R,B) 超过 40 且在中值绿色 110 以内的每个边界连接像素。钥匙只能从边框处，否则深色衣服会漏。
- 添加 2 px 软 alpha 带并将 G 钳位到其中的 max(R,B) + 6，这会消除绿色边缘。
- 按图形和掉落斑点对碎片进行分组。给每个精灵命名，然后给我看一张命名的联系表。

无臂的正面人物变成了木偶：
- 将头部在颈部分开：头部下方最窄的 alpha 行。
- 找到肩窝和眼窝。
- 用身体本身的颜色修补头下的洞，这样点头就不会出现间隙。
- 将所有内容写入 rig.js：尺寸、颈部、插座、眼框、皮肤 RGB、袖子 RGB。
- 手臂：上L1约为人物高度的0.13，下L2约为0.12，厚度约为0.04。对肘部和前臂皮肤使用袖子颜色，当手臂位于身体后方时，使用 0.82 倍深的袖子，以及圆形帽和连接处。
- 手：三种形状的连指手套（手套、张开、拳头），加上一根手指伸出的点。
- 手臂姿势：每个都是相对于肩膀的手部目标，单位为L = L1 + L2，通过二骨IK解决（其中有两个标志，第一个是左臂）。
- 向下：(∓0.04, 0.97)
- 休息：（±0.1，0.9）
- 臀部：(∓0.42, 0.55) 用拳头
- 点：右手到（0.86，-0.32）
- 现在：右手到（0.75，0.25），打开
- 耸肩：(∓0.62, 0.12)，打开
- 向上：(∓0.32，-0.9)
- 双手放在头上
- 下巴：拳头放在脖子上
- 保持：（±0.42，0.45）
- 波：（0.5，-0.75）
- 停止：(0.55，-0.1)
- 欢呼：（∓0.55，-0.75）用拳头
- 姿势变化在 0.3-0.5 秒内通过缓入缓出混合两个目标。
- 侧面、背面和姿势精灵保持完整图像。只有头部转动，绘图或打字的手抖动±6 px。
</钻>

<动画>
一个 HTML 画布，其中每一帧都是时间 t 的纯函数：window .seek(t)、READY、END 和 EV，按名称列出的声音事件列表。
- 将每个镜头挂在旁白上：S('exact Words', fn) 在该短语之前 0.08 秒开始一个镜头。重复的单词按出现次数查找。
- 每个镜头一个功能，每个章节一个镜头文件。

运动基元（Δ = t - 开始）：
- 弹出：0.3 秒后缓超调，1 + 2.9(p-1)^3 + 1.9(p-1)^2。
- 弹簧输入：1 - e^(-6.5Δ) cos(13Δ)。
- 冲击力踢：1 + 0.1 e^(-10Δ) cos(22Δ)。
- 摇动：x = A e^(-8Δ) sin(61Δ)，y = A e^(-8Δ) cos(47Δ)。
- 退出时间随着缓入时间的延长而缩小，时间超过 0.25 秒。事物到来时会伴随着春天、南瓜或白色的泡芙，而不是简单的褪色。

相机：
- camP（plate，zoom，fx，fy）将视图保持在板边缘内。
- 每个镜头都会通过缓入、2-4% 的推力或缓慢的平移从一个 [zoom、fx、fy] 移动到另一个，因此没有什么是静止的。
- 在同一相机变换内绘制盘子及其上的所有内容。
- 将四块图块上的缩放保持在 1.33 倍以下。仅在英雄板块上进行更深入的缩放。

过渡：
- 推：旧镜头从左侧滑出，新镜头从右侧滑入，0.24 秒缓入，之前有 0.02 秒的嗖嗖声。
- 章节 splat：#f4f1fb 斑点在 0.2 秒内覆盖屏幕并在 0.2 秒内清除。它是一个 1,250 像素的圆圈，由 12 个黄金角间距的大卫星斑点和更远的 10 个小水滴组成，在进入时向左移动 120 像素，在离开时向右移动 140 像素。

每一帧都充满活力的人物：
- 呼吸：标度 1 + 0.009 sin(2.3t)。
- 点头：0.025 sin(2.1t) rad，或 0.025 sin(7t) + 0.02 sin(11.3t)，同时说出该角色的台词。
- 闪烁：每 2.7-4.2 秒，每个数字播种。在 0.14 秒内，用弯曲的睫毛线将每个眼框涂上肤色。
- 步行：
- 鲍勃|罪|位于人物高度的 2.2% 处，主体岩石为 ±0.035 rad。
- 侧视行走精灵每个步循环滑动 1.5 条腿长，因此脚不会滑行。
- 进入泉水，有时会跳跃。恐惧是一种快速的震动（sin 70t）。惊喜是一个跳跃和一个橙色的“！”。
- 每个人物下方都有一个柔和的接触阴影椭圆。夜间拍摄的照片会用亮度 (1 - k) 使它们变暗，因此它们与车牌相匹配。
- 屏幕上的每个角色都按照自己的路线行事：指向被命名的事物，展示它，耸肩，欢呼，抬起头。
</动画>

<图形>
文本只存在于世界上的事物上，逐个字母地输入：每秒 28 个字母（短标签为 34 个）。每个字母以 1.45 倍大和向右 0.7 倍高度开始，并在 0.18 秒内稳定下来并缓出。

完整套件：
- 板：白色圆形板（半径 20），在弹簧上下降 420 px，摆动 0.25 rad 到位，或者站在木柱上，从 -1 rad 向上摆动。
- 柔和的阴影（模糊 22、y 8、22%）和沿其底部边缘的微弱深色条带。
- 输入的行之间间隔 0.3 秒。
- 日期卡：左上角 (70, 70)，白色，高 120 像素，宽至少 330 像素，半径 18。橙色日历图标，26 像素处有灰色“日期：”，以 44 像素粗细 900 输入日期。弹出时间超过 0.32 秒。
- 地点卡：带有红色地图图钉和“地点：”的同一张卡。
- 标签：一条 6 px 线，在物体上有一个点，在 0.2 秒内绘制，然后在其末端弹出一个圆形药丸（40 px 粗细 900 的文本）。墨水、红色、金色或橙色药丸。
- 号码卡：一张白色卡片，上面有一个灰色的小标签和一个红色的大数字。长数字像带有缓出功能的计数器一样滚动。
- 红色 X：两个圆形 30 px 笔划，每个 0.11 秒，间隔 0.01 秒，带有柔和的阴影。人们要仔细检查每一个错误的想法。
- 印章：双圆边框中的红色文本，倾斜 -0.12 rad。它在 0.14 秒内从 2.1 倍猛烈撞击到 1 倍，然后踢动。
- 横幅：全宽标题带，92 像素白色番茄或紫色帽子，旋转 -0.02 rad，从左侧滑入 0.22 秒。
- 语音气泡：白色，半径36，有尾巴。思想云：一颗有两个小圆圈的药丸。
- 橙子 ”？”它在一个困惑的头上晃动和摇摆，还有一个橙色的“！”流行音乐。
- 白色的云彩、速度线、浅蓝色的汗滴、硬币和钞票、柔和的小插图以及适合心情的色调。
- 只要该地方有空白板、屏幕和页面，就可以在该板块自己的空白板、屏幕和页面上书写。首先在板的网格覆盖层上测量毛坯的矩形。
</图形>

<声音>
- ElevenLabs：深度、温暖的美国纪录片旁白，eleven_v4，稳定性0.5，相似度0.75，风格0，扬声器增强，带有时间戳端点。
- 大约每分钟 170-180 个单词，使用语音自身的速度设置 (1.0-1.1)。永远不要用 Atempo 加快速度：听起来很花哨。
- 长脚本分为 3 个块，在章节中断处分割，传递上一个和下一个文本，以便阅读保持连续。
- 将 0.24 秒以上的停顿削减至 0.16 秒，在章节休息处留出 0.5 秒，并添加 0.3 秒的导入时间。
- 将对齐方式重建单词时间到words.js。
- 运行速度更快，在构建图片之前仔细研究结果并将其与脚本进行比较。
- 免费路线：Kokoro，然后更快地耳语单词时间。
</语音>

<声音>
- 音乐：Pixabay 上的 2-3 张免费纪录片床，以大节奏交叉淡入淡出超过 3 秒。
- 将音乐隐藏在声音下方（30 毫秒起音，0.3 秒保持，0.45 秒释放）并让它在章节之间回升。
- 来自 Mixkit 的 SFX，每个事件一个，按峰值对齐，语音时安静 6 dB：打字时的打字声、推动和敲击时的呼啸声、标签和卡片上的流行声、邮票上的重击声、每个红色 X 上的敲击声、滴答声上的叮当声，以及适合场景的声音。
- 门限：在演讲期间，声音比音乐加 SFX（100 毫秒帧的中值）高 15+ dB，并且背景比帧中的声音大 1%。
- 两次通过响度至 -14 LUFS，真实峰值 -1 dB。
</声音>

<构建>
1. 工具：Python、Playwright with Chromium 或 Edge、FFmpeg、faster-whisper、OpenCV、Pillow、numpy。安装缺少的内容并告诉我您安装了哪些内容。
2、订购：
- 外观测试
- 分批创作，每批之后都有一张联系表
- 剪裁和装备
- 语音和单词时间
- 镜头，逐章
3. 在任何完整渲染之前进行检查：每章一张联系表，每 2 秒一帧。修复：
- 空的或溢出的标志
- 脸上的文字
- 黑色板边缘
- 脚浮离地板
- 在同一个地方连续射击两次
- 任何没有新内容到达的 4 秒
4. 以 30 fps 渲染，半帧上有 4 个运动模糊子帧，帧通过管道输送到 libx264 CRF 16-18。
- 将长视频分割到 4-6 个并行浏览器页面并连接各个部分。
- 扫描单帧跳转的结果并检查每一帧是否是计划的剪切。
</构建>

<陷阱>
- 读起来很懒的地方太少了。一个盘子能保持 30 秒，上面有卡片，看起来很便宜。预算大约每分钟 10 个新位置。
- 一些图像模型忽略“没有手臂”。 GPT 图片 2 紧随其后。
- 将相同的角色描述粘贴到每张纸中，然后将底纸放回原处，否则脸部和衣服会漂移。
- 四块图块的宽度仅为约 1920 像素。突破 1.33 倍看起来很软。
- 已经画有人物的图版无法进行动画处理。切割前要求清空并检查。
- 漂浮在艺术作品上方的卡片上的文字看起来像幻灯片。写下这个世界。
- 长时间渲染崩溃。渲染可以重新运行的部分，并在每个大补丁之前备份镜头文件。
</陷阱>

- 切勿保持静止超过 1 秒。永远不要有不动的角色。

禁止：
- 轮廓、漂浮在艺术上方的光滑 UI 面板、表情符号、内置字幕
- 任何频道的标志或名称、真人照片
